clue.text: Fight that's often fatal for sheep

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or scuffle
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A deadly battle that sheep usually lose.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: the answer is a brain disease of sheep that usually kills.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a degenerative nervous disease of sheep and goats, usually ending in death.

clue.text: With South, North had developed a quick put-down

indicators.note: developed means grown into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In bridge, North and South develop a quick insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put-down' looks like an insult; it means something written down, quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a rapid system of writing that lets speech be taken down fast.

clue.text: The French king and queen comprehend the way to revel noisily

indicators.note: comprehend in its sense of contain, so the royal pieces enclose the way

parts.note: roi is French for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The French royal couple understand how to party loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehend' means 'contain' here, not 'understand'.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate boisterously and noisily.

clue.text: Flower much sought after by the French

definitions.meaning: a small red-flowered plant of fields

definitions.text: much sought after by the French
definitions.meaning: the elusive hero of Baroness Orczy's novel, sought everywhere by French revolutionaries

explanation.surface: A bloom the French prize highly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet one of the novel rescued aristocrats from the guillotine: 'They seek him here, they seek him there.'
explanation.definitionFit: It is a wild plant with small scarlet flowers, and the nickname of Orczy's daring fictional rescuer.

clue.text: Lionel Barrymore's part in the Exile's Retreat

indicators.note: part means only a portion of these words is taken

explanation.surface: An actor plays a role in a film about an exile's hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The exile is Napoleon, banished to this Mediterranean island in 1814. 'part' looks like an acting role but signals a hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba was the island where Napoleon lived in his first exile.

clue.text: Reported warning on the main page

indicators.note: reported means the phrase that follows is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: a bell buoy is a floating bell that warns ships at sea (the main is the open sea)

explanation.surface: A warning printed on the main page of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the sea, not a front page; 'page' is the hotel servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel page is a uniformed boy who runs errands and carries luggage for guests.

clue.text: Undisguised crook shared bunk

parts.note: bald means plain and undisguised, as in a bald statement

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or faulty, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A blatant criminal shared a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal and 'bunk' a bed; both shift sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk, short for bunkum, means nonsense, as does balderdash.

clue.text: There are said to be cracks in these greens

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the cracks

parts.note: leaks are cracks through which water escapes

explanation.surface: Rumour has it these vegetables are cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeks are green vegetables of the onion family.

clue.text: Military unit ordered to capture equipment

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A force commanded to seize kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an army formation made up of several battalions.

clue.text: Truly a way to raise dough

parts.note: yea is an old word meaning truly or indeed
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Honestly, a method of making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests money, but it is bread dough, which this makes rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus baked into bread to make dough rise.

clue.text: Political head leaves the platform in disfavour

indicators.note: leaves means the head letter departs from the word for the platform

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party leader steps down from the rostrum, out of public favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgrace, the state of being out of favour.

clue.text: The whole of Ireland is after the bishop with a dancing girl

indicators.note: is after puts the pieces for the whole of Ireland after the letter for the bishop

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the whole means all
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish bishop accompanied by a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: It is consuming the church's donations

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: Something that eats up the money given to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithes were tenths of produce or income paid to support the church and clergy.

clue.text: The main points found in a bulletin

parts.note: the main points of the compass are north, east, west and south, abbreviated N, E, W, S
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: The key points of a report appear in a bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast news bulletin on radio or television.

clue.text: Blonde not susceptible to such a timid one

definitions.text: Blonde not susceptible to such a timid one

parts.words: Blonde not susceptible to such a timid one
parts.note: plays on the proverb that a timid suitor never won a fair lady, the blonde of the clue

explanation.surface: A fair-haired woman is unmoved by a shy admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs '___ never won fair lady'; 'Blonde' stands for the fair lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint-heart is a timid, cowardly person lacking courage.

clue.text: Article about the professional stage

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article encloses the professional

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a pro is a professional

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the professional theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage that projects in front of the curtain.

clue.text: She escaped from Rock, now stars in the north

definitions.text: She escaped from Rock, now stars in the north

parts.words: She escaped from Rock, now stars in the north
parts.note: the Greek princess chained to a sea rock and freed by Perseus, who gives her name to a northern constellation

explanation.surface: A woman who broke out of a rock-bound prison is now a star.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth she was chained to a rock as an offering to a sea monster and rescued by Perseus; the gods placed her among the stars of the northern sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is both the rescued princess of Greek myth and a constellation of the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: The two sides are oceans apart when business is slack

indicators.note: apart means held separate, so the two sides are pushed apart by the oceans

parts.note: in cricket the two sides of the field are the off side and the on side
in cricket the two sides of the field are the off side and the on side
seas are oceans

explanation.surface: Two teams separated by oceans during a quiet trading spell.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket field is split into an off side and an on side; 'apart' is the container signal, the oceans sitting between those two.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-season is the quiet part of the year when trade or tourism falls away.

clue.text: Genuine hit tune new in the bill

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the bill

parts.note: a/c is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A real hit song appears on the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives UTHENTI, an anagram of the song words; 'bill' means account, not a programme or invoice in the theatrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real and of undisputed origin.

clue.text: Odd details about the north east where and when things happen

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the compass piece
odd suggests the letters are in a strange order and need rearranging

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Strange particulars about the north-east of where events take place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' gives DATELIS, the anagram, which then goes round the compass point; the definition describes the line heading a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A dateline at the head of a report gives the place and date it was written.

clue.text: Browning's defeat?

definitions.meaning: going brown, as skin does in the sun

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Browning is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter points to the poet Robert Browning, but here it is simply turning brown; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanning means turning brown in the sun, and colloquially a thrashing or heavy defeat.

clue.text: Mock loud fellow with rough manners

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a lout is a crude, ill-mannered man

explanation.surface: Ridicule a noisy, uncouth man.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout is to openly scorn or treat with contempt, as in mocking a rule.

clue.text: How to bowl if you lift the elbow?

definitions.text: How to bowl if you lift the elbow?

parts.words: How to bowl if you lift the elbow?
parts.note: a cricket bowling style with the arm brought round above the shoulder, where the elbow rises past the arm

explanation.surface: Cricket coaching advice about raising the elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's arm comes over the shoulder; 'lift the elbow' also suggests drinking, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Overarm bowling delivers the ball with the arm swung above shoulder height.

clue.text: Rolls up at tea-party?

parts.note: pictures bread rolls squaring up for a fight, and also guests rolling up to a social gathering

explanation.surface: Guests arrive at a tea-party.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a tea-party is called a fight over the buns; 'Rolls up' reads as arriving, but rolls are also buns.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunfight is a humorous British term for a tea-party or crowded social function.

clue.text: Small object on radar screen round Minehead is a balloon

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the radar spot encloses the head letter

parts.note: a blip is a spot of light on a radar screen
the head of mine is its first letter, M; Minehead is also a Somerset seaside town

explanation.surface: A radar blip over the seaside town of Minehead turns out to be a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a Somerset seaside town, but read as 'mine head' it gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, a kind of large balloon.

clue.text: Anger rising in French girl

parts.note: ire means anger

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the French word goes backwards

parts.note: en is French for in

explanation.surface: A French girl's temper flares up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' in a down clue reverses EN into NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name.

clue.text: Deny one left 23, say, to retire

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to retire means to go back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A man denies that someone left the 23rd to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is IRENE; 'one left' removes I to give RENE, and 'to retire' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or refuse to honour an undertaking.

clue.text: Farm boss

definitions.meaning: a farm where horses are bred
a knob or ... standing out from a surface, as on a shield

explanation.surface: The man who runs the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a horse-breeding establishment, and a raised ornamental knob like a boss.

clue.text: Moving from circuit to circuit, I preach noisily without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first pieces go round the point

parts.note: to rant is to hold forth loudly
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A travelling preacher shouts his sermons without making any point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside': I and RANT surround TINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant judges and preachers travel a circuit, moving from place to place.

clue.text: Little vessel in the way

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the abbreviation for way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A small boat blocking the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient or meagre, small in amount.

clue.text: Paint model, tempting when topless

indicators.note: model as a verb means to shape, so the letters are reshaped
topless means the word loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A painter's model is tempting when posing topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes T off 'tempting' to give EMPTING, which 'model' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a colouring substance, the base of paint.

clue.text: Large numbers in the police retire when active

indicators.note: retire means draw back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in places the large numbers inside the police abbreviation

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
many means a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of police officers retire while still in service.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police; 'retire' reverses the whole container, giving the run read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means energetic and forceful, full of activity.
